title: Skeletal Phenotyping in Complex Musculoskeletal Diseases: A Retrospective Analysis of Bone Density, Microarchitecture and Structural Parameters
summary:
This study aims to improve our understanding of bone health in people with complex musculoskeletal diseases. We will analyze bone scans (DXA scans) that were performed as part of routine medical care to assess bone density, bone structure, and bone quality. We will also review information from medical records and routine laboratory tests.

No additional examinations or study visits are required, and no new tests will be performed. By comparing bone characteristics across different diseases, we hope to better understand how these conditions affect the skeleton and to support the development of improved diagnostic and treatment strategies for future patients.
conditions: Complex musculoskeletal diseases are conditions that affect the bones, joints, muscles, or tendons and are often associated with changes in bone strength or bone metabolism. These include, for example, rare bone diseases (such as osteogenesis imperfecta, X-linked hypophosphatemia, or hypophosphatasia), osteoporosis, inflammatory or genetic skeletal disorders, and other diseases affecting the musculoskeletal system.

interventions.name:
To characterize skeletal phenotypes in patients with complex musculoskeletal 
diseases based on bone density, microarchitecture, and structural parameters through retrospektive patient data analysis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a clinically and/or genetically confirmed complex musculoskeletal disease.
Availability of DXA examinations performed as part of routine clinical care with analyzable datasets for bone mineral density (BMD), trabecular bone score (TBS), and/or structural bone parameters (3D-Shaper)  from 2023 on.
Availability of complete baseline clinical data (e.g., age, sex, and diagnosis).
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete or non-analyzable DXA imaging data.
Missing essential clinical data required for the planned analyses.
